clue.text: Switch witless, regressive escape plan

indicators.note: read as 'wit less': the word switch loses the letters of wit
going backwards, so the synonym for escape is read in reverse

parts.note: to escape is to elude

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly backtracks on a plan to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'witless' strips WIT from SWITCH to leave SCH; 'regressive' turns ELUDE into EDULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable or programme of events is a plan, so the noun swaps cleanly.

clue.text: Belt, suit and kit comes off here!

parts.note: a belt of land is a narrow strip
clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A list of clothes, belt and suit and kit, then the punchline that they all come off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kit' looks like a third clothing item in the list, but it belongs to the definition: clothes are removed in these venues.
explanation.definitionFit: Venues where performers undress are the places where clothing is taken off, a playful cryptic description.

clue.text: Desirable accommodation the Spanish scrubbed

indicators.note: scrubbed means cancelled or removed, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: a hotel provides accommodation
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: Sought-after lodging where the Spanish guests have been struck off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in great demand or fashionable is described as hot in informal use.

clue.text: Questionable nature of bishop that is in charge

indicators.note: the bishop and 'that is' letters go in the word for charge

parts.note: a duty is a charge or responsibility
B is the chess notation for bishop
i.e. abbreviates id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Doubts about a bishop's character, said to be in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtfulness or uncertainty is the quality of being questionable, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Making acceptable gaol? In time, it collapses

indicators.note: something that collapses falls apart, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A prison, given time, falls down, suggested as a way to make it acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something lawful or justified is the act of rendering it acceptable.

clue.text: Ring opera company about Shakespearean role

indicators.note: the opera company's letters go about the character's name

parts.note: ENO is English National Opera
Prince Hal appears in the Henry IV plays

explanation.surface: Call an opera company about a part from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like 'phone', but it is the verb meaning to encircle with a halo.
explanation.definitionFit: To surround with a halo is to ring or encircle something with light.

clue.text: Round Uist's borders, catch island's sea creatures

indicators.note: the synonym for catch goes round the edges of the Scottish isle

parts.note: to nail a criminal is to catch them

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Around the coasts of Uist, someone catches the island's marine life.
explanation.walkthrough: Uist is an island in the Outer Hebrides; its borders give UT, which goes into NAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: These cephalopods with spiral chambered shells live in the sea, so they are an example of sea creatures.

clue.text: Believer's role is a help, off to secure job

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the word for job inside them
off means wrong or awry, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a post is a job

explanation.surface: Advice that a helping hand is lacking when trying to get a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off to secure job' reads like setting off to land a job, but 'off' is the anagram signal and 'secure' means hold around.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of one of Christ's disciples or a fervent follower is the role of a devoted believer.

clue.text: Sign suggesting an absence of people?

parts.note: O is zero, nothing, a total absence
men stands for people in general

explanation.surface: A sign that hints at a deserted place.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or augury is a sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Ditch, a secure area for kind of root

parts.note: a rut is a groove or ditch
to bag something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A trench and a fenced-off patch, where a certain root vegetable grows.
explanation.walkthrough: RUTABAGA is the American word for swede, the yellow root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Swede is a root vegetable, so it is one kind of edible root.

clue.text: Storm warning around ancient city

indicators.note: the golfer's warning goes around the old city

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An alarm raised about a storm near an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar or public outcry is a storm, as in a storm of protest.

clue.text: Register in store about good on-line traffic?

indicators.note: the register, in and store letters go about the abbreviation for good

parts.note: a roll is a register of names
stock is a store of goods

explanation.surface: Signing up to an online shop about some good internet traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on-line' is not the internet: it means on the railway line, and the traffic is trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotives and carriages are the vehicles that move along a railway line, its traffic.

clue.text: Person who's demanding to inspect fire training

indicators.note: training shapes something into a new form, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone exacting comes along to inspect a fire drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists on flawlessness is a demanding person to work for.

clue.text: Tender women carelessly giving another gift

definitions.note: a gerund phrase for the noun act of making a fresh endowment

indicators.note: carelessly suggests the letters thrown together in a jumble

explanation.surface: Kind-hearted women handing out presents without thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh endowment is a new donation or gift to an institution, given again.

clue.text: Wow! Magical creature's hugging boy in film

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: the magical being's letters wrap around the boy

parts.note: a fairy is a magical creature; the 's reads as 'is'
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Amazement as a fairy cuddles a boy in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1964 musical starring Audrey Hepburn is a well-known film.

clue.text: Cautious line taken by US general

indicators.note: the line abbreviation is taken on by the general, following him

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
RY abbreviates railway, a line

explanation.surface: A careful route chosen by an American general.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wary or suspicious is to be cautious.

clue.text: Labourer, dressing badly, with yen for hats

indicators.note: the labourer's letters dress, or clothe, the word for badly

parts.note: a miner is a labourer
ill means badly, as in ill-treated
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A poorly dressed worker with a yearning for headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' reads as a longing, but it is the currency, giving Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade of making women's hats, and its products, means hats collectively.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory porcelain for activity in court

parts.note: bad means unsatisfactory
Minton is a brand of English porcelain

explanation.surface: Poor-quality china presented as evidence in a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court; it is the badminton court.
explanation.definitionFit: This racket sport is played on a court, so it is an activity in a court.

clue.text: Topless dance captivates individual playwright

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold, so the remaining letters hold the next word
topless means without its top letter

parts.note: a disco is a dance
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A topless dancer enthrals one particular dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' takes D from DISCO to leave ISCO, which holds ONE. Eugène Ionesco was a Romanian-French absurdist playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionesco wrote The Bald Soprano and Rhinoceros, so he is a playwright.

clue.text: Small drink's drunk with unobtrusive sound

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: cha is tea, a drink

explanation.surface: A small drink downed with a quiet sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles CHA and W into CHWA. The schwa is the neutral vowel heard in the first syllable of 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: The schwa is the weak unstressed vowel, the least prominent speech sound in English.

clue.text: Touring currently, get lost in vehicle for winter

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the get-lost word goes round the next one

parts.note: scat! means go away
now means currently

explanation.surface: A traveller told to clear off while touring in a winter vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracked vehicle for snow travel is a vehicle for winter conditions.

clue.text: Person jumping on kind of software browser?

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense the jumper comes on after, following the software

parts.note: Windows is Microsoft's operating system
a hopper is one who hops or jumps

explanation.surface: Someone leaping on a particular web browser program.
explanation.walkthrough: 'browser' suggests web software; it is someone who looks in shop windows without buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone looking at displays without buying is browsing, a browser of goods.

clue.text: Month gets cold and damp, needing to turn up heat

indicators.note: in a down clue to turn up is to read upwards, backwards

parts.note: raw weather is cold and damp

explanation.surface: A cold, damp month means turning up the heating.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat something is to warm it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: A guy giving command for soldier

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them

explanation.surface: A man giving an order to a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a noun for a man; it is the verb meaning ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: The order to relax stance is a drill command given to soldiers.

clue.text: Criminal drilling precious metal, a source of wealth

indicators.note: the criminal bores into the metal, going inside it

parts.note: gold is a precious metal
a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A crook boring into gold, a source of riches.
explanation.walkthrough: Golconda, the old Indian city famed for diamonds, means a mine of wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a fabled Indian diamond city came to mean any rich mine or source of wealth.

clue.text: Name tabs an indicator of first name?

definitions.text: Name tabs an indicator of first name?

parts.words: Name tabs an indicator of first name?
parts.note: the word means 'born' and is placed before a married woman's original family name

explanation.surface: Labels on a name badge showing a forename.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for born introduces a woman's maiden, original surname, her first family name.

clue.text: System satisfied stretcher bearer

parts.note: met as in met the requirements, satisfied
a hod is a builder's trough carrying bricks, a stretcher being a brick laid lengthwise

explanation.surface: An orderly arrangement satisfied the man carrying the stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretcher' suggests a medical litter; it is a brick laid lengthways, carried in a hod.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a procedure or system for doing something.

clue.text: Restless Cockney striker screened by broadcaster

indicators.note: screened means enclosed, so the striker sits inside the broadcaster

parts.note: Sky is a British broadcaster
a Cockney drops the H, so a hitter becomes 'itter

explanation.surface: An agitated London footballer shown on a TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, the London accent, drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Being jumpy or skittish means being restless.
